title: Ringed pro-etale open extension preserves products and Roos triangles
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-open-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $R_U=j^{-1}R$, and use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $J=D(j_!)$ for termwise exact ringed extension by zero [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. For every countable family $C_n\in D(R_U)$, the canonical morphism $J(\prod_n C_n)\to\prod_n JC_n$ is an isomorphism, whose $n$th projection is $J$ of the original projection. For every inverse system $(C_n,d_n)$ and every distinguished Roos triangle $C\xrightarrow{c}\prod_n C_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n C_n\to C[1]$ [def-weil-inverse-system] [def-weil-derived-limit], applying $J$ and these canonical product isomorphisms gives a distinguished Roos triangle $JC\to\prod_n JC_n\xrightarrow{1-s_J}\prod_n JC_n\to (JC)[1]$ for the transitions $Jd_n$. Its first map has components $J(c_n)$, where $c_n$ is the $n$th component of $c$. No constructibility, boundedness or constant-ring hypothesis is imposed.
